summary: @servicetitan/mfe-quick-actions preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, writes it to a temp path, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a ~727KB Bun-compiled bundle whose contents are obscured with string-array-shuffle obfuscation (a large numeric/string constants table plus a rotating accessor function, mangled _0x/MmgoCP identifiers). Executing this payload via a freshly-downloaded runtime evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code paths. The published purpose is a React/mobx micro-frontend (dist/index.js is a normal MFE bundle); there is no legitimate reason for a UI micro-frontend to fetch an alternate JS runtime at install and execute an obfuscated sibling script under it. The publisher-purpose mismatch, alternate-runtime dropper mechanism, and opaque install-time payload are consistent with a compromised maintainer credential or malicious republish under the @servicetitan scope. On default npm install, the preinstall lifecycle hook auto-executes the obfuscated payload on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
